problems.title: Digit sum after factoring large powers
problems.question: Find the digit sum of (21·8⁸·5²²−7·8⁷·5²²)/(2³·3−1).
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
formulas: Factor out $7\cdot8^7\cdot5^{22}$; combine equal powers of 2 and 5 into powers of 10.
steps: The remaining numerator factor is 3×8−1=23, exactly the denominator. The quotient is 7×2²¹×5²²=35×10²¹.
Its decimal form is 35 followed by 21 zeros, giving digit sum 3+5=8.

problems.title: A perpendicular through an intersection
problems.question: Find the line perpendicular to y=4x+19 through the intersection of 3x−y=1 and y−5x=7.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
steps: The two lines are y=3x−1 and y=5x+7, so x=−4,y=−13.

problems.title: Domain of a composed rational function
problems.question: f(x)=2/(x−1), g(x)=x f(x−3)/(x+1). Find the real domain of g.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
formulas: All denominators must be nonzero, including those inside a composition.
steps: f(x−3)=2/(x−4), excluding x=4. The outside denominator excludes x=−1. There are no other restrictions.

problems.title: A rational system becomes linear
problems.question: Solve 2/(2x+y)+3/(x−y)=25/14 and 3/(2x+y)−1/(x−y)=−1/14.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
steps: Thus 2x+y=7 and x−y=2. Adding gives 3x=9, so x=3,y=1. Both original denominators are nonzero.

problems.title: Minimum distance to the x-axis
problems.question: A=(a²+4a+5,a²+6a+11). For which real a is its distance to the x-axis least?
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
formulas: Distance to the x-axis is the absolute value of the y coordinate; $a^2+6a+11=(a+3)^2+2$.
steps: The y coordinate is always positive. Its minimum 2 occurs exactly at a=−3.

problems.title: Graph branches and count horizontal intersections
problems.question: Graph f(x)=2x−6 for x<1 and f(x)=−x+8 for x>3. Find all a for which f(x)=a has two roots.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
formulas: The first branch has range $(-\infty,-4)$; the second has range $(-\infty,5)$.
steps: Draw the ray y=2x−6 ending with an open dot at (1,−4), and the ray y=−x+8 starting with an open dot at (3,5). No graph lies over 1≤x≤3.
Each branch is one-to-one. A horizontal line meets both exactly when a lies in both ranges, namely a<−4.

problems.title: Two exterior secants and an arc ratio
problems.question: A,B,C,D lie in that order on a circle. Rays AB and DC meet outside at 20°. Arcs AD:BC=7:3. Find the arcs.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
formulas: Exterior secant angle = half the difference of the far and near arcs.
steps: The far arc AD minus near arc BC is 40°. Write them as 7t and 3t: 4t=40°, giving t=10°.
The arcs are AD=70° and BC=30°.

problems.title: A cyclic quadrilateral forces perpendicular lines
problems.question: The incircle of ABC with centre O touches AB,BC at M,N. Line MN meets A’s bisector at K; O,N,K,C are concyclic. Find AKC.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
formulas: Radius ON is perpendicular to tangent NC; opposite cyclic angles are supplementary.
steps: ONC=90°. Since O,N,K,C lie on a circle, OKC=90° as well.
A,O,K are collinear because O lies on A’s bisector. Therefore KC is perpendicular to AK, giving AKC=90°.

problems.title: A midpoint of an arc and two crossing chords
problems.question: A,B,C,D lie in order on a circle; N is midpoint of arc AB. NC and ND meet chord AB at E,K. NDC=45°. Find KEC.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
formulas: An inscribed angle halves its arc; a chord-intersection angle halves the sum of its opposite arcs.
steps: Let arcs AN=NB=t. NDC=45° gives the arc NC not containing D as 90°; this arc passes through B.
The opposite arc AC not containing N is 360°−(t+90°)=270°−t. The ray EK points toward A because the chord order places K between A and E.

problems.title: A factorization reveals a thirty-degree angle
problems.question: Right-triangle sides satisfy a<b<c and 3ac+bc−c²−2a²−2ab=0. Find the angles.
problems.idea: Simplify the data to a standard relation and retain the domain or geometric conditions.
steps: The triangle inequality gives a+b−c>0, so the other factor must be zero: c=2a.
c is the hypotenuse and a the shortest leg. A leg half the hypotenuse is opposite 30°. The other acute angle is 60°.
